problem: The chapter says lexicalization lets the grammar use 'telescope' and 'fork' to choose the attachment, but its own head rules make the preposition the head of the PP ('PP takes the preposition'). Under those rules the PP 'with the telescope' is headed by 'with', so 'telescope' and 'fork' are never heads of a child of the deciding rule and never enter P(A → B C | a, b, c). Part (b) of the worked example correctly uses 'saw' and 'man', so the lead and Q2 contradict the rest of the chapter.
fix: Name the heads that actually condition the rule: the verb, the noun and the preposition. Say: a plain PCFG cannot weigh the triple (saw, man, with) against (ate, pizza, with), because the words do not enter the rule probability. Words inside the PP such as 'telescope' are not heads under these head rules. Change Q2's answer to 'the words saw, man and with do not change the fixed rule probabilities'.

problem: The reduce is written 'REDUCE-BINARY-RIGHT as NP → [NP(boy)]', with the rule left unfinished; a student cannot see which rule fired.
fix: Write 'REDUCE-BINARY-RIGHT as NP → Det N, giving NP(boy); the noun boy is the head'.

problem: 'REDUCE-BINARY-LEFT as VP → [NP(boy), VP(ate)]' mixes the rule with the stack after the move. Read literally it shows the rule VP → NP VP, which is not in the grammar given.
fix: Write 'REDUCE-BINARY-LEFT as VP → V NP, head ate from the left child V; the stack becomes [NP(boy), VP(ate)]'.

problem: The prose says a shifted word becomes a tagged preterminal (Det(the), V(ate), N(cake)), but the figure and the dry-run table show bare words ('ate', 'the', 'cake'). The trace is also labelled REDUCE-R in the table and REDUCE-BINARY-RIGHT in the prose.
fix: Use one form throughout: Det(the), N(boy), V(ate), N(cake), NP(boy), VP(ate), S(ate), with the action names SHIFT, REDUCE-BINARY-RIGHT, REDUCE-BINARY-LEFT, FINISH in both the figure and the table.

problem: The caption says the marked cell is the most recent item (the top of the stack), but row 3 ('REDUCE-R NP') carries an unexplained 'accent' mark that is not the top of the stack.
fix: Drop the accent mark, or state in the caption that it marks the subtree just built.

problem: 'Det takes the determiner' presents Det as a phrase that percolates a head from a child. Det is a preterminal, so it has no head child; its head word is the word itself.
fix: Replace with: 'A preterminal such as Det or N has no head child; its head is its word. Phrase rules percolate: S and VP take the verb, NP takes the noun, PP takes the preposition.'

problem: 'Reading REDUCE-BINARY-LEFT/RIGHT as the side of the stack' is unclear; students may read 'side' as the left or right edge of the stack rather than as which of the two popped subtrees supplies the head.
fix: Write: 'Reading LEFT/RIGHT as the direction of attachment. The label names the child that supplies the parent head: LEFT means the left of the two popped subtrees is the head, not that the phrase attaches to the left.'
